newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's Marshall aims to raise 97 sales 10 pct.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Marshall aims to raise 97 sales 10 pct.

text.p: Turkey's leading paint, varnish and glue producer Marshall Boya ve Vernik Sanayii A.S. aims to increase its total sales by 10 percent in 1997 from $133 million in 1996, a senior company official said.

"We exceeded our 1996 sales target by six percent to $133 million and we plan to grow at least 10 percent this year," Mehmet Ozbalak, assistant general manager of the company, told Reuters in an interview.

Ozbalak said the company planned to increase exports by more than 100 percent in 1997 from 331 billion lira in 1996, and aimed to raise them to 10 percent of total sales in three years from 2.4 percent in 1996.
Marshall increased its total production by four percent in 1996 from a total 70,517 tonnes of paint, varnish and glue in 1995.
The company has annual 70,733 tonnes of paint, 32,673 tonnes of varnish and 29,627 tonnes of glue production capacities.
Ozbalak said they would continue small-scale investments to overcome bottlenecks in some production lines through capacity expansion projects.
"We have enough production capacity to meet market needs, but investing to equalise all stages of the production process helps us increase productivity," he said.
He said Marshall controlled 25 percent of the domestic market in 1996 and the DYO group of Yasar Holding, including Yasas, controlled 26 percent.
Other domestic producers -- CBS with 10-12 percent and Polisan with five to six percent and smaller ones -- shared the rest of the market, he added.
Total sales of the company increased to 13.7 trillion lira in 1996 from 7.6 trillion lira in 1995 and net profit rose to 1.1 trillion lira from 328 billion.
